verify-277-season-mechanics.summary: Verified against #277's contract (Gama's final ready comment) at HEAD in mvox-app. The season-manage surface is a single page-level $state pair bound to exactly one auto-picked season, with no per-season list and no season-switch guard on any in-flight write. All five requested points confirmed with file:line evidence below.

findings.claim: manageableSeasonId / selection logic / page-level $state / panel binding
findings.evidence: Pure pick: src/lib/attendance/conductorLogic.ts:104-116 `manageableSeason(seasons, now)` — current-if-not-lapsed, else soonest not-yet-started (by startDate, '' sorts last), else the lapsed current, else null. Its own doc (lines 88-99) names the exact gap #277 closes: 'the shape is a season SELECTOR in the manage panel... not further tuning of this automatic pick.' Wired once per load in src/lib/agenda/agendaData.ts:92-99 (`listFullAgenda`) into `manageableSeasonId`/`Owners`/`Editors`. Page-level $state declared at src/routes/+page.svelte:347-348 (`manageableSeasonId`, `manageableSeasonRights`), set from the load's `.then()` at +page.svelte:853-855, blanked to null/'not-editor' at +page.svelte:1124-1125 (loadForSelected reset). The panel binds to it: `openSeasonManagePanel()` (+page.svelte:2995-3067) guards on `manageableSeasonId === null` (line 3000), captures `const seasonId = manageableSeasonId` (line 3014) for its three fetches, and the render gate `showSeasonCard` (+page.svelte:2610-2612) is `manageableSeasonId !== null && manageableSeasonRights === 'editor'`. There is exactly ONE such id/rights pair on the whole page — not a map keyed by season.

findings.claim: manageableSeasonRights derivation, consumption, and what carries across a season change today
findings.evidence: Derived at +page.svelte:854-855 as `manageRightsFrom(mOwners, mEditors, personId)`, plus a DB-entity-rights fallback (+page.svelte:896,913-920, `loadDatabaseEntityRights`) that promotes it to 'editor' when the season's own `_owner`/`_editor` are invisible (private-bucket absence — the 'Mihkel case', #167 review F2/F3). Consumed at: `showSeasonCard` gate (2610-2612); every field-edit/conductor-add/remove write guard (`confirmSeasonFieldEdit` 3193, `onSeasonManageConductorSelect` 3270, `onSeasonManageConductorRemove` 3287, via `manageableSeasonId === null` checks); passed straight through as `seasonRights={manageableSeasonRights}` to the panel's RepertoireElement (+page.svelte:7336) with the comment 'the panel is unreachable without it, so no separate rights check is needed here' (7314-7315). Nothing 'carries across a season change' today because there is no season-change event to carry across: `manageableSeasonRights` is a single flat $state, wholesale-overwritten on every `loadFullAgenda()` resolve (853-855) or blanked on reset (1125). The rights-derivation logic itself (manageRightsFrom + the async DB-entity fallback) lives inline inside that one `.then()` callback, not in a function callable per-arbitrary-season, so switching the managed season client-side (without a full agenda reload) has nothing to call to re-derive rights for the newly chosen season.

findings.claim: the season card list render / where a per-season entry affordance attaches / [+ Hooaeg] relocation from #261
findings.evidence: There is no season CARD LIST in the codebase — grep for season-card/SeasonCard/seasons.map across all .svelte files returns only src/routes/+page.svelte. It is ONE card (`data-testid="agenda-admin-card"`, +page.svelte:5970), rendered under `{#if showSeasonCard || seasonManageOpen}` (5969), bound to the single `manageableSeasonId`. Collapsed, it renders ONLY the season name via `seasonManageDeleteName` (+page.svelte:6017, derived 2686-2690 as `seasons.find(s => s.id === manageableSeasonId)?.name`) inside one native `<h2><button data-testid="season-card-expand">` (6004-6019) per #261's ruling ('collapsed season card displays only the name... gear not needed'). Opened, it shows a title row (collapse control + trashcan, 6034-6067) then the panel body (fields, series, events, repertoire). The `[+ Hooaeg]` control (`data-testid="season-create"`, +page.svelte:5924-5934) sits directly ABOVE this one card, gated on `showSeasonCreate && !seasonCreateOpen` alone (#261 comment 5909-5923: 'LEAVES the card and stands here, above it, as its own page-level control... whenever an upcoming season exists too'). A per-season entry affordance for #277 has nothing existing to extend into a list — it would replace this single collapsed-button block with an iteration over the manageable subset of `seasons` (already available with owners/editors per-entity, see next finding), one collapsed entry per season, each independently opening the SAME shared panel state re-pointed at that season's id.

findings.claim: panel state that would be stale on a season switch: repertoire section, series rows, in-flight writes
findings.evidence: Enumerated stateful pieces, all declared +page.svelte:2614-2629,2722,2816,2939-2940,4784: `seasonManageOpen`, `seasonManageName/StartDate/EndDate/ConductorIds`, `seasonManageFieldsLoaded`, `seasonManageSeries`, `seasonManageEvents`, `seasonManageSeriesError/EventsError`, `seasonManageDeleteGeneration`, `seasonEditingField`, `panelRepertoire/Works/Editions/Copies`, `panelPendingKeys`, `panelRepertoireError`, `seriesCreateSeasonId` (5277: seeded from `manageableSeasonId` at open, not re-derived). Concrete staleness bug found: `openSeasonManagePanel()` only re-seeds name/start/end/conductor fields `if (!seasonManageFieldsLoaded)` (+page.svelte:3003-3012) — that boolean is NOT keyed to a season id, so a close (`closeSeasonManagePanel`, 3069-3112) followed by a reopen for a DIFFERENT season leaves the OLD season's name/dates/conductors on screen until an edit overwrites them; only the full `resetSeasonManage()` (2892-2941, called on collective switch / agenda-load failure, NOT on panel close) clears `seasonManageFieldsLoaded` back to false. Series/events/panelRepertoire ARE unconditionally re-fetched on every `openSeasonManagePanel()` call (3044-3066, `loadPanelRepertoire` at 2960-2993) using the freshly captured `seasonId`, so those self-heal on next open — but only IF `openSeasonManagePanel()` is re-invoked; nothing currently re-runs it on a mid-session season switch. In-flight writes are the sharper risk: `confirmSeasonFieldEdit` (3192-3224), `onSeasonManageConductorSelect` (3269-3284), `onSeasonManageConductorRemove` (3286-3298) all capture `const seasonId = manageableSeasonId` for the wire call but their `.then()`/`.catch()` apply optimistic-revert / pending-clear to the shared, non-season-keyed `seasonEditPending`/`seasonManageConductorIds`/`seasonEditErrors` state UNCONDITIONALLY — none of them re-check `manageableSeasonId === seasonId` on resolve. If a season switch happens while one of these is in flight, its resolution will mutate whatever season's fields are now displayed. The codebase's only reusable staleness-guard idiom for this exact shape is `seasonManageDeleteGeneration` (declared 2722, bumped only in `resetSeasonManage` at 2914, checked at 2732/3914/4077/4090/4095) — built for the delete-cascade only; the page-level `requestId`/`thisRequest` pattern used elsewhere (e.g. loadPanelRepertoire 2961,2965,2969) guards collective switches, not season switches within the same collective, since `requestId` does not bump on a season change.

findings.claim: the only-one-season-manageable common case: what determines the manageable set, and what 'no new control for the common case' means for the render
findings.evidence: Today the code computes at most ONE manageable season, never a set (`manageableSeason()` returns `Season | null`, conductorLogic.ts:104). For #277 to expose several, the natural set is 'every season the viewer holds rights on, filtered to not-lapsed/upcoming' — and the data for that already rides along for free: `listSeasons` (src/lib/seasons/entuSeasons.ts:101-102,189-190) attaches `owners`/`editors` to EVERY season in the list, not just the picked one, and `agendaData.ts`'s `FullAgendaResult.seasons` (field doc at agendaData.ts:26-35, wired +page.svelte:827 `seasons = fullSeasons`) already carries the full list into page state with zero extra fetch. So `manageableSeasonRights`'s per-season DB-entity-rights fallback (the 'Mihkel case', +page.svelte:896,913-920) is the one piece NOT free — it runs today only for the single auto-picked season and would need to run per-candidate season to keep the set correct when a season's own rights props are invisible. On rendering: 'no new control for the common case' (issue's 5th Done-when: 'the existing behaviour is unchanged when only one season is manageable') means that when the computed manageable SET has exactly one member, the render must degenerate back to today's single collapsed-name button (+page.svelte:6004-6019) with no picker/list chrome and no visible 'switch season' affordance at all — concretely, whatever new per-season-list markup replaces that block needs a `set.length === 1` branch (or the list simply renders as one entry indistinguishable from today's single button) so the common case's DOM and interaction stay byte-identical to the current one-card behaviour, and the visible-only-when-plural labeling criterion ('states which season it is managing... whenever more than one is manageable') is the same conditional.

verify-277-guard-idiom.summary: At HEAD (5bf94a8, after #287/#296/#297/#299/#300) there are TWO separate implementations of the same generation-guard idiom, not one. Roster/library/profile share the routeLoad.ts machine (src/lib/loading/routeLoad.ts, createRouteLoadMachine). The home page src/routes/+page.svelte — which is also where all season-management code lives — does NOT use routeLoad.ts at all; it hand-rolls its own page-local generation counters (`requestId`, plus a second finer one `worksLoadId`/`scheduleLoadId`, plus a season-delete-cascade-specific one `seasonManageDeleteGeneration`). The idiom's SHAPE (capture-before-await, compare-after-await, guard the write) is identical across both, but there is no shared season-scoped helper, and no season-switch event exists today to hook a guard onto — only a collective switch does, because #167 restricts management to exactly one derived season, not a user-pickable one.

findings.claim: The generation-guard idiom's canonical shape is: capture the counter into a local before the write's await, then compare the captured value against the live counter immediately after settle, returning early (dropping the write) on mismatch — spelled either `if (g !== routeLoad.generation) return;` / `if (!routeLoad.isCurrent(g)) return;` (roster/library/profile) or `if (thisRequest !== requestId) return;` (home page).
findings.evidence: src/lib/loading/routeLoad.ts:90-92 defines `isCurrent(g)`; roster fix commits (859f6a4 #287, 8122e3c #297, d158b09 #299) all capture `const g = routeLoad.generation;` (or `gEntry`) at handler entry before the first await, e.g. src/routes/roster/+page.svelte:2044,2069,2110-2121 (`const g = routeLoad.generation;` ... `if (g !== routeLoad.generation) return;` before each state write in the .then/.catch/.finally chain). Independently, src/routes/+page.svelte:636 `let requestId = 0;` and dozens of sites like line 821/915/947/983/1268/1717/2317/2965 do `const thisRequest = requestId;` (or `++requestId` at a genuine switch, line 729) then `if (thisRequest !== requestId) return;` before each assignment.

findings.claim: The idiom is implemented by exactly one SHARED unit (routeLoad.ts's createRouteLoadMachine, exposing `.generation`/`.isCurrent(g)`) used by roster, library and profile pages, plus InviteSurface.svelte — but the home page (+page.svelte, which hosts all season-management UI) is a second, independent, hand-rolled implementation that does not import or call into routeLoad.ts at all.
findings.evidence: `grep -rl routeLoad src` returns src/lib/loading/routeLoad.ts, src/lib/components/admin/InviteSurface.svelte, src/routes/library/+page.svelte, src/routes/profile/+page.svelte, src/routes/roster/+page.svelte — NOT src/routes/+page.svelte. `grep -n "createRouteLoadMachine|routeLoad|reset:|isSwitch" src/routes/+page.svelte` returns zero matches. Home page instead defines its own `let requestId = 0` (line 636), `let worksLoadId = 0` (654), `let scheduleLoadId = 0` (660) and `let seasonManageDeleteGeneration = 0` (2722), each a plain (non-`$state`) module-scope counter, copy-guarded inline at every write site rather than through a shared function.

findings.claim: Within the season-management region of +page.svelte, the guard sites that are reusable-in-shape for a season-switch guard are the page-local `requestId`/`seasonManageDeleteGeneration` sites already scoped to season-manage state (loadPanelRepertoire, makeSeasonManageDeleteProgress, the delete-cascade completion checks at 4077/4090); the roster-side routeLoad.ts guard sites (#287/#296/#297/#299/#300 fixes) are collective-switch-and-roster/library-specific and not directly reusable for a season switch, since they live on a different page/machine entirely and key off collective (db) identity, not season identity.
findings.evidence: season-manage sites live only in src/routes/+page.svelte (e.g. resetSeasonManage 2892-2941, makeSeasonManageDeleteProgress 2728-2735, loadPanelRepertoire 2960-2993, delete-cascade guards at 4077/4090/4095) and all key off `requestId`/`seasonManageDeleteGeneration`, both page-local to +page.svelte. The #287/#296/#297/#299/#300 fixes are entirely inside src/routes/roster/+page.svelte and src/routes/library/+page.svelte, keyed off `routeLoad.generation`/`routeLoad.isCurrent(g)` from a machine instantiated per-page against `selected()`'s `db` (routeLoad.ts:98 `current?.db`) — i.e. collective identity. No season-manage code path reads or writes `routeLoad.*`, and no roster/library code touches `seasonManageDeleteGeneration` or `requestId`.

findings.claim: Reset-on-switch today is triggered by direct, non-generic call sites inside loadForSelected() in +page.svelte (both the deselection branch and the normal-selection branch call resetManagement() and resetSeasonManage({dropConvertRun:true}) inline, keyed on collective/db change), NOT through a registered reset-callback/effect the way routeLoad.ts's `reset` option works for roster/library/profile. No equivalent SEASON-switch hook point exists: management is restricted by #167's design to exactly one derived `manageableSeasonId` (soonest current-or-future season) per collective load — there is no season picker, no `selectedSeasonStore`, and no code path where the user changes which season is being managed without also changing collective.
findings.evidence: src/routes/+page.svelte:671-797 loadForSelected() directly calls `resetManagement()` (line 689, 744) and `resetSeasonManage({dropConvertRun:true})` (line 708, 769) inline in its two branches — contrast with routeLoad.ts:58 `reset?: (info) => void` which is a registered option invoked once at the top of `loadForSelected` inside the shared machine (roster's `createRouteLoadMachine({..., reset: (info)=>{...}})`). Searching for any season-switch construct (`seasonPicker|SeasonPicker|selectedSeasonStore|manageSeasonId|switchSeason`) across src returns nothing. openSeasonManagePanel (line 2995-3000) reads `manageableSeasonId` — a value re-derived per collective load from `deriveSeasonCreateRights`'s ladder (lines 1179-1196) — with no setter exposed to the UI for picking a different season while staying on the same collective. Issue #277 (gh issue view, read for scoping only) is literally proposing that a 'manage-any-upcoming' season picker would be one way to resolve this — confirming the hook point does not exist yet.

findings.claim: An existing test already pins the collective-switch generation-guard behavior for the season-delete cascade in the exact page-local (`requestId`/`seasonManageDeleteGeneration`) style RED for a season-switch guard would need to mirror: switch the driving store mid-write, assert the stale in-flight write's UI effect disappears immediately, then resolve/tick the stale promise and assert it produces no effect (no resurrection, no reload, no announcement).
findings.evidence: src/routes/page.season-manage-delete.spec.ts:1484-1528 'a collective switch mid-cascade clears the counter — and a late tick from the abandoned run never resurrects it' — sets `selectedCollectiveDbStore.set('org-b')` mid-cascade, asserts `season-manage-delete-progress` becomes null, then calls `run.tick(3,9,'event')` after the switch and asserts it stays null. A second test at 1530-1573 pins the completes-after-switch case (no reload count bump, no status text). Both are in src/routes/page.season-manage-delete.spec.ts (co-located with +page.svelte, same file naming convention as the roster/library collective-switch specs at src/routes/page.roster-*-collective-switch.spec.ts and src/routes/page.library-bulk-checkout-collective-switch.spec.ts, all siblings under src/routes/).

verify-290-font-site.summary: Repo guard passed (mvox-app.git). Verified #290's final ruling (group 1 only, PO-approved 2026-09-09) against HEAD (5bf94a8). The cited line/classes match exactly, but the ruling's factual premise about what that line displays is wrong: it is the event name, not a member's name. No font-body/font-sans utility exists to swap to — the fix should just drop font-display, matching the sibling body-text convention already in the file. No other font-display use in the file, and no test breaks.

findings.claim: Line 203 of AttendanceSurface.svelte currently reads `{item.name}`, exactly as quoted in Mihkel's ruling comment.
findings.evidence: Read at src/lib/components/attendance/AttendanceSurface.svelte:203 (HEAD 5bf94a8). git blame shows this line unchanged since commit e4df8920 (2026-08-10) — no drift since the ruling was written.
findings.implication: The literal edit target (swap the class) is unambiguous and safe to apply as written.

findings.claim: The ruling describes line 203 as rendering 'a member's name ... in the column a conductor reads down while marking P/A/L' — the load-bearing justification for calling this group 1 (the readability-critical instance).
findings.evidence: Line 203 renders `item.name`, where `item: AgendaItem` (the Props interface at line 32) — this is the agenda item/event, not a roster member. It sits in the panel HEADER row next to the close button (lines 202-214), before the P/A/L roster even starts. The actual member name the conductor reads while marking P/A/L is a SEPARATE span at line 240: `{member.name}` — which has NO font-display class at all, and never has (only one font-display occurrence exists in this file, confirmed by `grep -n font-display` over the whole file: line 203 alone).
findings.implication: The change as specified (swap font-display off line 203) is real and harmless to make, but it fixes a mislabeled target: it removes handwriting styling from the EVENT NAME in the panel title, not from a roster member's name. The member-name readability concern the ruling used as its deciding argument does not actually exist in this component — that span was already in the body face. The one-line exception comment required by the ruling should describe the TRUE site (event name in the panel header, group-2-shaped: text you already know, not misread-risk member text) rather than restate the ruling's 'member's name' framing, or a later reader will be confused by a comment that doesn't match what the code renders.

findings.claim: The app has a distinct 'body face' utility (e.g. font-body/font-sans) that sibling non-display text uses, which the fix at line 203 should adopt.
findings.evidence: src/app.css defines exactly three font tokens under @theme (lines 60-62): --font-sans: 'Inter', system-ui, sans-serif; --font-mono; --font-display: 'Caveat', cursive. There is no font-body utility anywhere (grep across src/ found none). Sibling non-display text in this same component — member name (line 240), RSVP label (241), load-error text (231), row save-failed text (293), tally line (302) — all use plain text-sm/text-xs/text-[10px] with NO font-* class at all; none of them write font-sans explicitly (grepped the whole src tree, zero hits for the literal class font-sans). app.html/+layout set no explicit body font either — Inter is simply what renders when no font-display/font-mono class is applied.
findings.implication: The correct fix is to DROP font-display from the class list entirely (leaving `truncate text-sm text-ink`), not to add a font-sans/font-body class — that matches the established convention every other body-text span in this file already follows. Adding an explicit font-sans would be inconsistent with the file's own pattern, though functionally identical.

findings.claim: font-display appears more than once in AttendanceSurface.svelte, so other sites need checking for accidental touch.
findings.evidence: grep -n "font-display" src/lib/components/attendance/AttendanceSurface.svelte returns exactly one line: 203. Nothing else in the file uses font-display.
findings.implication: There is nothing else in this file to accidentally disturb — the diff for #290 should touch exactly one line.

findings.claim: Some test/spec asserts on the classes of the line-203 span, or otherwise renders AttendanceSurface in a way that would break on a class swap.
findings.evidence: Grepped every spec touching AttendanceSurface (page.attendance-a11y.spec.ts, page.attendance-inline-placement.spec.ts, page.event-create-collapse.spec.ts, page.ux-polish-i18n.spec.ts, event/[id]/page.i18n-a11y.spec.ts, event/[id]/page.spec.ts, AttendanceSurface.scroll.spec.ts, AttendanceSurface.ghost.spec.ts). All target the panel/rows via data-testid selectors (attendance-panel, attendance-row-*, attendance-toggle-*, attendance-panel-loading/error) or scrollIntoView call args — none select or assert classes on the bare, testid-less header span at line 203. page.ux-polish-i18n.spec.ts lists this file among CHANGED_SURFACES but only scans for hardcoded text nodes / i18n key parity / outline-none focus-strip hygiene — {item.name} stays an expression node and no outline/focus class is touched by a font-display->plain swap, so that scan is unaffected.
findings.implication: The class swap is safe to make with no test fallout; no test needs updating alongside the fix.

findings.claim: There is an established house idiom for a deliberate-exception comment (the third done-when item in the ruling) that the #290 fix should follow.
findings.evidence: Two existing examples sit in this very file, both from the #151 typography pass: lines 227-230 (surface-level error role comment: 'text-sm text-red-700, the treatment every other whole-surface load failure uses (library, admin, invite, auth). This was text-ink-2, which rendered a failure in the same colour as ordinary body copy, and its sibling SeasonSummary rendered the same role at text-xs.') and lines 288-290 (row-level error role comment: 'text-xs text-red-700, as everywhere else. text-[9px] is the stamp/badge tier (font-mono uppercase chips); an error sentence is body copy, not a stamp.'). The shape: `<!-- #<issue> — <what this class choice is/does>: <chosen class(es)>, <contrast with what it is NOT and why>. -->`, placed directly above the element, one issue number, one sentence of rule plus one sentence of contrast.
findings.implication: The #290 exception comment should follow this exact shape and should state the true referent — item.name / event name in the panel header — rather than repeat the ruling's 'member's name' description, e.g.: '#290 — this is the event name in the panel's own title row (item.name), not a roster member's name; it stays in the body face on purpose, not the display face used for identity elsewhere.'

blast-277-axes.summary: Blast-radius sweep for #277 (per-season management) done from /home/ai-teams/workspace-app (origin confirmed mvox-app.git). Core finding: manageableSeasonId/manageableSeasonRights are single flat page-level $state in src/routes/+page.svelte, consumed only there plus the pure picker in conductorLogic.ts and the producer in agendaData.ts — no other component reads them. Rights ARE per-season (Season.owners/editors are per-entity _owner/_editor refs), so divergence across seasons is real and already coded, not vacuous. Season-switching does not exist yet, and the codebase's existing collective-switch guards (requestId, seasonManageDeleteGeneration) do not cover a season-only switch — several in-flight panel writes capture manageableSeasonId at submit time and settle against that stale captured value with no live re-check, which is exactly the shape that produced #287/#296/#297/#299 on the roster page for collective switches. Locale keys for season management exist and are in parity across en/et/lv/uk, but nothing exists yet for a 'which season is this' label — a new key is needed in all four.

findings.claim: Every unit test for manageableSeason() pins a SINGLE-season pick, including the literal #277 scenario (a running season plus a later upcoming one) — these tests describe the AUTOMATIC DEFAULT pick and likely extend rather than flip.
findings.evidence: src/lib/attendance/conductorLogic.manageable.spec.ts:39-45 — 'a current season exists alongside FUTURE seasons -> still the current one'; every case in the file (lines 33-117) asserts one `?.id`. src/lib/attendance/conductorLogic.ts:104-116 `manageableSeason()` returns `Season | null`, never a list. src/lib/agenda/agendaData.spec.ts:359-402 and src/lib/testing/agendaFixtures.ts:56-93 pin the producer's single manageableSeasonId/Owners/Editors triple the same way.
findings.implication: Gama's ruling asks for a way to CHOOSE, not a different default pick — these pins should stay green as the initial/fallback value; new tests are needed for the override path, not edits to these.

findings.claim: manageableSeasonId/manageableSeasonRights have exactly one consumer surface: src/routes/+page.svelte (one flat panel bound to one id). No other component or route reads them.
findings.evidence: grep for `manageableSeason` across src (excluding spec files, conductorLogic.ts, agendaData.ts, agendaFixtures.ts) returns zero hits outside src/routes/+page.svelte. All ~70 in-file usages (declared src/routes/+page.svelte:347-348) are read/write sites inside that one file: the card gate `showSeasonCard` (line 2610-2612), the panel open/close/field-edit/conductor/delete/repertoire/series-create functions (lines 3000-5784), and the rights derivation in the agenda load (lines 853-855).

findings.claim: Season rights are read per-SEASON-entity (Season.owners/editors are that season's own visible _owner/_editor refs), so per-season rights divergence between two upcoming seasons is genuinely possible in the current model — not something the criterion invents.
findings.evidence: src/lib/seasons/types.ts:24-35 — Season.owners/editors documented as `_owner`/`_editor` refs VISIBLE to the reading caller, per entity. src/routes/+page.svelte:854-855 — `manageableSeasonRights = manageRightsFrom(mOwners, mEditors, personId)`, where mOwners/mEditors come from the manageable Season's own arrays (agendaData.ts:92-97). src/lib/repertoire/repertoireActions.ts:291-297 — `manageRightsFrom` is `owners.includes(personId) || editors.includes(personId)`, a pure per-entity-arrays check with no org-level lookup.
findings.implication: Done-when criterion 4 is sound and will exercise real divergent data. Caveat: src/routes/+page.svelte:896-929 has a DATABASE-ENTITY rights fallback that grants collective-wide 'editor' whenever a season's own owner/editor arrays come back EMPTY — for someone holding only that DB-level grant, every season looks like 'editor' regardless of per-season grants, so divergence is only demonstrable for people with direct season-level grants.

findings.claim: On a COLLECTIVE switch (and every same-collective loadForSelected() reload — season/event/series create, any panel write that reloads), manageableSeasonId/manageableSeasonRights are blanked SYNCHRONOUSLY via resetManagement(), even reloads that keep the panel open (keepSeasonManage:true). No season-scoped equivalent exists for a user-driven switch between two already-loaded seasons, because that operation doesn't exist yet.
findings.evidence: src/routes/+page.svelte:744 `resetManagement();` runs unconditionally inside loadForSelected before the `if (!keepSeasonManage)` branch at line 745; resetManagement() (lines 1121-1136) sets `manageableSeasonId = null` and `manageableSeasonRights = 'not-editor'`. Comment at lines 3592-3594 confirms this explicitly. resetManagement()/resetSeasonManage() are called only from loadForSelected's call sites (lines 689, 708, 744, 769, 962, 977) — never from a path that would fire on a same-collective, panel-open season switch.

findings.claim: The codebase has a precedent generation-guard idiom for collective switches (requestId; the delete-specific seasonManageDeleteGeneration) that Gama's ruling names as the pattern to reuse — but it is applied inconsistently even today, and covers nothing season-only.
findings.evidence: requestId declared src/routes/+page.svelte:636, bumped line 729, checked at many sites (821,915,947,983,992,996,1004,1013,1017,1268,1274,1325,1330,1350,1373,1380,1450,1462,1468,1717,3024). seasonManageDeleteGeneration declared line 2722, bumped only inside resetSeasonManage (line 2914). onSeasonManageSeasonDelete (lines 4053-4097) guards BOTH its `.then()` (line 4077) and `.catch()` (line 4090) with an explicit 'operator switched collective mid-cascade' comment; onSeasonManageSeriesDelete (lines 4006-4039) only guards its `.finally()` (line 4037) — its `.then()` success handler (lines 4017-4030) unconditionally mutates seasonManageSeries/seasonManageArmedSeriesCount/seasonManageDeleteStatus and calls refreshAfterSeasonManageDelete(cfg) with the OLD cfg; onSeasonManageEventDelete (lines 4099-4120) has NO generation guard anywhere.

findings.claim: Season field edit and conductor add/remove capture manageableSeasonId at call time but their completions carry NO guard (no requestId, no live manageableSeasonId re-check) before mutating shared, non-season-keyed page state; and the one-time field-seed flag is never reset on a season-only switch. Failure scenario: admin renames season A (optimistic apply + write in flight), switches panel to season B before settle; the stale .then()/.catch() then mutates seasonEditPending / reverts seasonManageName against what is now B's displayed row. Separately, unless the switch code clears seasonManageFieldsLoaded, switching to B for the first time renders A's cached name/dates/conductors under B's heading because the reseed guard `if (!seasonManageFieldsLoaded)` (line 3004) thinks fields are already loaded.
findings.evidence: confirmSeasonFieldEdit (src/routes/+page.svelte:3192-3228) captures `const seasonId = manageableSeasonId` (line 3210), then its `.then()`/`.catch()` (lines 3216-3225) unconditionally set seasonEditPending/applySeasonFieldLocally(field, before)/seasonEditErrors with no guard. onSeasonManageConductorSelect (3269-3283) and onSeasonManageConductorRemove (3286-3296) — same shape, no guard on the `.catch()` mutating seasonManageConductorIds/seasonManageConductorError. seasonManageFieldsLoaded (line 2619) is reset only inside resetSeasonManage(), never invoked on a same-collective season-only switch.

findings.claim: submitEventCreate and submitSeriesCreate capture panelSeasonId = manageableSeasonId at submit and compare it only against the form's target seasonId at completion — never against the LIVE manageableSeasonId at settle time — which is exactly the invariant a season switch would break. Failure scenario: admin creates an event targeting season A while panel manages A (match at submit), switches the panel to B before settle; completion still sees the stale match and calls refreshSeasonManageLists(cfg,'A'), overwriting the panel's series/events lists with season A's data while the panel now displays season B — reproducing the exact bug this code's own comment says it exists to prevent, via a route it never anticipated.
findings.evidence: src/routes/+page.svelte:4573 and :5543 capture panelSeasonId, explicitly because resetManagement() blanks manageableSeasonId mid-reload (comments 4567-4571, 5539-5542). Usage at line 4717: `if (origin === 'panel' && panelSeasonId === seasonId) { refreshSeasonManageLists(cfg, panelSeasonId); }`, with design comment at 4713-4716 stating this exists so a form-target-season mismatch doesn't 'swap the OTHER season's rows in under the panel's heading.' Same pattern at lines 5751-5752 and 5781-5783. The comparison is always against the captured panelSeasonId, never re-read live.

findings.claim: refreshPanelRepertoire (the #234 panel repertoire section) already re-checks the LIVE manageableSeasonId, not just a captured copy, before applying its result — a working template for the guard the other paths above are missing.
findings.evidence: src/routes/+page.svelte:1710-1723: `const seasonId = manageableSeasonId; const thisRequest = requestId; listRepertoireItems(cfg, seasonId).then((items) => { if (thisRequest !== requestId || manageableSeasonId !== seasonId) return; panelRepertoire = items; })`.

findings.claim: The season-manage panel today is ONE global card/panel gated by a single boolean (showSeasonCard), with no per-season card and no season-list UI — confirming a picker/per-season entry point is genuinely new UI, not free.
findings.evidence: src/routes/+page.svelte:2606-2612 — `const showSeasonCard = $derived(manageableSeasonId !== null && manageableSeasonRights === 'editor');` — a single boolean gating the whole card, not a per-season list.

findings.claim: All four locales (en/et/lv/uk) carry the identical 35 season_manage_* keys in parity, but none names or references 'which season is being managed' — #277 criterion 2 needs at least one brand-new key added to all four, not a reuse.
findings.evidence: grep '"season_manage[a-z_]*"' across messages/en.json, messages/et.json, messages/lv.json, messages/uk.json returns the identical 35-key set verbatim in every file; none names or holds a slot for a season identifier/label.

blast-289-autosave-inventory.summary: Repo guard passed (origin=mvox-app.git). Read-only sweep of src/ in ~/workspace-app for epic #289. The app has NO <form>/onsubmit anywhere (grep confirmed zero hits) — every write in mvox is fired from onclick/onchange/oninput/blur/idle-timer, so the auto-save class is large. Found four generic write-orchestration queues (rsvpChangeQueue, attendanceChangeQueue, profileEditQueue, and a shared createRepertoireWriteQueue reused by repertoire-management AND event-field-editing) that all share the same shape: setPending fires synchronously, a settle callback either reconciles or rolls back, primary double-tap guard is the UI disabling the control, backstop is an in-queue Set. Three of the four are OPTIMISTIC (value shown before the write lands); profileEditQueue and the roster_show_real_names/collective-name pair are server-confirmed. Across every surface except #267 (roster_show_real_names), there is no POSITIVE 'saved' signal — success just clears the pending/error flags, so a saved value and a never-attempted value render identically once the pending flag clears. Two surfaces (library inline checkout/return, admin add/remove admin+librarian) have NO pending indicator and NO double-tap guard at all, though both are server-confirmed via refetch so they cannot lie, only stay silent. One surface (profile name/email autosave) deliberately preserves the unsaved draft on failure (by design, to not lose typing) while showing a role=alert error — compliant with the epic's 'never leave a value on screen without saying so' AC, but still lacks a 'saved' announcement. Section drag-reorder in roster/+page.svelte is the SECOND full exemplar (after #267): it has an explicit pending copy, a real 'moved' success announcement, and a truthful failure/partial-failure distinction. Excluded from the inventory: language/agendaView/timeFormat prefs (localStorage only, no server write), section rename and member-record edits (explicit Enter/Save-button commit, not silent auto-save), invite creation on admin/invite (explicit 'Create' button), and member deactivate/remove (two-step explicit confirm gesture).

findings.claim: Exemplar #267 mechanics, verified from source: src/routes/profile/+page.svelte onRosterNamesChange (lines 847-894) plus the sr-only status region (997-1011).
findings.evidence: rosterShowRealNames is assigned ONLY inside the .then after `await updateRosterShowRealNames` resolves (line 882) — never optimistically. rosterBusy=true disables the

findings.claim: RSVP (member Going/Not going): optimistic, silent-pending, no positive saved cue.
findings.evidence: src/lib/rsvp/rsvpChangeQueue.ts request(): setPending(eventId,true) (line 83) then setOptimistic (line 87) BEFORE the write — the button already shows the new status while the POST is in flight. src/lib/components/agenda/RsvpControl.svelte: pending disables all 4 buttons + aria-busy, but per an explicit PO ruling captured in the component's own header comment (lines 10-13) shows NO 'saving' text — 'silent-disable, no saving text'. On success, reconcile() (rsvpChangeQueue.ts:93-95) just swaps in the real rsvpId — visually identical to the pre-tap 'not yet attempted' state showing that same status. On failure, revert() (rsvpChangeQueue.ts:100-101) restores the exact pre-tap value and the page sets failedEventIds, which RsvpControl renders as a role=alert line ('rsvp-save-failed', RsvpControl.svelte:147-148). Two consumers: src/routes/+page.svelte (handleRsvpChange, 1073-1084, wired at line 8063) and src/routes/event/[id]/+page.svelte (line 3004 area). Not yet attempted and saved are visually indistinguishable — the exact 'dangerous pair' the epic names.

findings.claim: Attendance (conductor P/A/L per member): identical shape to RSVP, keyed by event+member.
findings.evidence: src/lib/attendance/attendanceChangeQueue.ts mirrors rsvpChangeQueue.ts line-for-line (module header at lines 5-17 states this explicitly): setOptimistic before the write (line 113), reconcile only clears pending (no positive signal), revert restores the pre-tap value. UI: src/lib/components/attendance/AttendanceSurface.svelte — aria-busy on the toolbar (line 261) + aria-disabled on the buttons (line 268) while pending, no visible text distinguishing busy from idle; failure renders a per-member role=alert line ('attendance-save-failed-{memberId}', lines 287-298). Wired from src/routes/+page.svelte (createAttendanceChangeQueue usage feeding AttendanceSurface's ontoggle). Same not-yet-attempted/saved ambiguity as RSVP.

findings.claim: Inline event-field editing on the event detail page (name, start_datetime, duration_minutes, location, description, event_type) is a full optimistic auto-save surface not named in the epic's seed list.
findings.evidence: src/lib/events/eventFieldEdit.ts updateEventField() — module header states plainly 'the caller (+page.svelte) is what turns [a throw] into an optimistic-revert + inline error'. src/routes/event/[id]/+page.svelte confirmFieldEdit() (lines 2089-2152): on blur/Enter, `applyFieldLocally(field, value)` runs via the `apply` hook of createRepertoireWriteQueue.request() (repertoireActions.ts:408-438) BEFORE the write resolves — optimistic. The pencil button disables (`disabled={editWritePending.name === true}`, e.g. line 2338) with opacity-40, no aria-busy, no text — same silent-disable shape as RSVP. On success, editErrors[field] is just set false (line 1812) — no positive 'saved' cue; the header already shows the new value from the optimistic apply. On failure, the `rollback` hook restores `before` (repertoireActions.ts:429-431, called before `revert`), then a role=alert line renders ('event-edit-error-name' etc., e.g. lines 2356-2360). Six fields, one shared generic queue, all six with this gap. This is a materially large surface the epic's seed list (RSVP/attendance/#267) did not mention.

findings.claim: Repertoire/programme management (season repertoire list + event program items: add work, add program item, status change, pin/ordinal move up-down, remove) shares the SAME generic optimistic queue and the SAME gap.
findings.evidence: src/lib/repertoire/repertoireActions.ts createRepertoireWriteQueue (408-438) is instantiated twice in src/routes/+page.svelte: `repertoireQueue` (line 1482) and `panelQueue` (line 1748). src/lib/components/agenda/RepertoireElement.svelte fires every action straight from onclick with no separate submit: handleRemove (line 453), handleStatusChange (501), handleMove up/down (520, 530), handleAddWork (562), handleAddProgramItem (598) — none of these sit behind a confirm step. The queue's own doc comment (repertoireActions.ts 386-407) confirms the optimistic-then-rollback shape verbatim ('Optimistic in the RSVP/attendance sense... local mutation lands synchronously on tap'). Same consequence as the event-field surface: no positive 'saved' signal, silent pending only.

findings.claim: Collective name (admin page) is server-confirmed (not optimistic) but still lacks a positive 'saved' cue — a partial match to the #267 exemplar.
findings.evidence: src/routes/admin/+page.svelte confirmNameEdit() (357-392): nameMarker is reassigned only inside the try block AFTER `await updateCollectiveName` resolves (line 374) — correctly server-confirmed, matching #267's discipline. nameWritePending disables the pencil (opacity-40, line 570/572) with no text. On failure nameError renders role=alert (591-595, 'admin-collective-name-error'). BUT there is no success announcement of any kind — the editor just closes and the pencil re-enables; a 'not yet attempted' first-view of the same name and a just-saved rename are pixel-identical. Same absence of a positive cue as the optimistic surfaces above, despite being correctly non-optimistic.

findings.claim: Profile name/email autosave (idle-timer + blur + visibility-change) is genuinely time/blur-triggered with no click at all — the purest auto-save surface in the app — and deliberately preserves an unsaved value on screen through a failure.
findings.evidence: src/lib/profile/autosave.ts createAutosave(): keystroke() arms a setTimeout(config.idleMs) (default 2000ms, wired at src/routes/profile/+page.svelte:713); blur()/visibilityChange() fire immediately. src/lib/profile/profileEditQueue.ts request(): setPending synchronous (line 83), reconcile ONLY after applyProfileSave resolves (line 91) — this queue is server-confirmed, not optimistic (comment at lines 11-14 states this explicitly: reconcile fires only in .then). BUT the on-screen value the whole time is `draft[field]` (profile/+page.svelte:1088, `bind:value={draft[field]}`), which was set at KEYSTROKE time via handleValueChange (797-800) — long before any save fires. profileEditQueue.ts's own doc (lines 41-42) states the caller 'KEEPS the draft (preserve-on-error)' on failure — i.e. a value that failed to save is intentionally left standing. This is compliant with the epic's AC only because ProfileField.svelte renders a role=alert error line simultaneously (line 368, saveFailed -> 'profile_save_error') — the false-looking value is accompanied by a loud error, not silent. No positive 'saved' cue on success (savingFields just clears, ProfileField.svelte 347-361 shows 'saving' text but nothing on completion).

findings.claim: Admin role management (Add/Remove admin, Add/Remove librarian) is a genuine native-<select>-onchange / button-onclick auto-save surface with ZERO pending indicator and ZERO double-tap guard.
findings.evidence: src/routes/admin/+page.svelte onPickAdmin/onPickLibrarian/onRemoveAdmin/onRemoveLibrarian (443-497): each awaits a write (addAdmin/removeAdmin/addLibrarian/removeLibrarian) and on error sets a single SHARED boolean `actionError` (not per-row). Markup (605-724): the <select> (line 652, onchange fires onPickAdmin directly) has no disabled-while-pending state, and neither Remove button (628-634, 710-720) is disabled during the await — only `!canManageAdmins`/`isLastOwner`/`isSelf` gate them, never an in-flight flag. There is no local `pending`/`busy` state variable for this whole block at all (confirmed via full $state grep of the file). Server-confirmed via refreshAdmins/refreshLibrarians refetch after success, so it cannot show a false 'saved' value, but a user gets ZERO feedback that anything is happening during the round-trip, and nothing stops a rapid double-click from firing two overlapping removes/adds.

findings.claim: Library inline checkout (assign a member to an available copy) and lending return are auto-save with the SAME 'zero pending indicator, zero double-tap guard' gap as admin roles.
findings.evidence: src/routes/library/+page.svelte, comment at lines 980-983 states outright: 'inline checkout: selecting a member on an available copy row checks it out immediately (no separate submit step). Server-confirmed.' handleInlineCheckout (984-1012) and handleReturn (1023-1041): neither sets any pending/busy flag before its `await createLending(...)` / `await returnLending(...)`; only `inlineCheckoutErrors` (a Map, per-copy) and `returnError` exist, and both are only touched on the error path. Full $state/const grep of the relevant block confirms no `checkoutPending`/`returnPending` variable exists. The <select> that drives checkout (onchange at line 1535) and the Return button (onclick at line 1572) stay clickable through the whole round-trip. Server-confirmed via a full lending-list refetch after success, so it cannot lie, but nothing tells the user a write is even in flight, and nothing prevents a double-fire.

findings.claim: Roster invite mint / withdraw-invite use ONE shared page-level pending boolean across all rows, not a per-row one, even though the error state IS per-row; unverified whether the buttons visually bind to it.
findings.evidence: src/routes/roster/+page.svelte: `inviteActionPending` (declared line 107) is a single boolean guarding both handleInviteMint and handleWithdrawInvite (1411-1436) — `if (inviteActionPending) return;` is the ONLY re-entrancy guard, shared across every roster row. `inviteErrorByMemberId`/`withdrawErrorByMemberId` (100-101) ARE per-member, so failures are attributed correctly. Server-confirmed via refreshJoinState after success (no optimistic join-state flip). Did not verify in this pass whether the mint/withdraw buttons visually bind `disabled={inviteActionPending}` per-row in the template (would need a template grep beyond this budget) — marked INFO rather than CONFIRMED that a second row's control stays visually clickable while another row's invite write is in flight, even though the shared boolean would make a second click silently no-op.

findings.claim: Section reorder (roster admin's arrange view, drag-and-drop and touch-drag) is the codebase's SECOND genuine four-state exemplar, comparable in quality to #267.
findings.evidence: src/routes/roster/+page.svelte: `reorderPending` (2460) disables the drag handles (`draggable="false"`, per comment 2456-2458); `reorderStatus` carries real, named success announcements — e.g. `m.roster_section_moved(...)` (2557, 3452), `m.roster_section_grabbed(...)` (3341), `m.roster_section_dropped(...)` (3351, 3369) — into a persistent sr-only role="status" region ('roster-reorder-status', line 4174). On failure it does NOT blindly revert to a stale optimistic snapshot: per the code comment at 2493-2513, it re-fetches sections from the server and renders whatever partial state actually landed, distinguishing a total failure (`m.roster_section_reorder_failed`) from a partial one (`m.roster_section_reparent_partial`, both rendered at line 4325) — truthful even under partial failure, which is stronger than every optimistic-revert surface above.

findings.claim: Section rename, the member-record admin editor (name/phone/email/birthdate/id_code), and invite creation on /admin/invite are NOT silent auto-save — each requires an explicit commit gesture — and are correctly excluded from the epic's scope.
findings.evidence: Section rename (roster/+page.svelte, markup comment at 4651-4652): 'no Save/Cancel buttons — matches the issue's literal contract' but commit is via Enter (onRenameKeydown -> submitRename, line 4663) — an explicit keyboard-submit gesture, not a silent side-effect of typing; well-covered anyway (renamePending/renameError/renameStatus, 2826-2834). Member-record editor (roster/+page.svelte 1497-1518, 3794-3797): has an explicit `data-testid="roster-record-save"` button with `onclick={() => saveRecordEditor(row)}` — a real Save button, server-confirmed, disabled while `recordSavingMemberId !== null`. Invite creation (src/lib/components/admin/InviteSurface.svelte, line 415 `onclick={submit}`) — an explicit 'Create invite' button. None of these three match the epic's 'auto-saving field' definition (a write fired by the interaction itself with no separate save press); flagging as REFUTED against the possibility they belong in the inventory, so sub-issue cutting does not mistakenly target them.

findings.claim: Language, agenda-view and time-format preference controls are local-only and never reach the server, so they carry no auto-save risk at all.
findings.evidence: src/lib/preferences/agendaView.ts and its spec (agendaView.spec.ts) confirm the store persists to `localStorage` key 'mvox.agenda_view' with SSR-safe guards; grep of src/lib/preferences/*.ts and LanguageSelector.svelte for entuFetch/fetch returned zero hits. There is no server write to distinguish four states for — the epic's 'four states' framing does not apply because there is no 'in the system' to be uncertain about.

findings.claim: The app has no <form>/onsubmit anywhere in src/, which is why the auto-save surface is as large as it is.
findings.evidence: `grep -rn "onsubmit\|type=\"submit\"" src --include="*.svelte"` returned zero matches across all 33 .svelte files. Every write-triggering interaction in mvox is an onclick/onchange/oninput/onblur/timer, which is precisely the epic's stated trigger surface ('control whose interaction triggers a server write WITHOUT an explicit save/submit press') — meaning the inventory above is close to exhaustive of ALL writes in the app, not a narrow subset, and any future write path added without a deliberate confirm-button decision will land in this same class by default.

blast-290-256-sweep.summary: REPO GUARD passed (origin=mvox-app.git). (A) Full suite baseline captured: 4241 passed / 1 failed / 4242 total tests (274/275 files green). findings.claim: No literal class-string / classList / toHaveClass assertions touch AttendanceSurface or font-display in any spec.
findings.evidence: grep of AttendanceSurface|font-display|toMatchSnapshot across all specs found only descriptive comments and render() calls (src/lib/components/attendance/AttendanceSurface.ghost.spec.ts, .scroll.spec.ts, src/routes/page.attendance-a11y.spec.ts, src/routes/page.event-create-collapse.spec.ts, src/routes/event/[id]/page.spec.ts, src/routes/page.attendance-inline-placement.spec.ts) — no `class="..."`, `classList`, `className`, `getAttribute('class')`, or `toHaveClass` assertions in those files (targeted re-grep returned empty). findings.claim: The closest existing collective-scoped child-list patterns are repertoire_item (season-child, CRUD-only) and section (collective/parent-child, CRUD + display_order reorder).
findings.evidence: Data-helper shape: src/lib/repertoire/repertoireData.ts:48-78 (listRepertoireItems, read-only) + src/lib/repertoire/repertoireActions.ts:62-87 (createRepertoireItem), :94-101 (updateRepertoireStatus), :108-115 (pinEdition), :118-125 (deleteRepertoireItem) — no display_order anywhere in this module (repertoire_item has no manual reorder; program_item's ordinal reorder is a separate mechanism at repertoireActions.ts:176-256, gated to program_item only). Contrast: src/lib/sections/sectionActions.ts:100-187 (createSection, explicit _type-as-reference + _parent + _sharing:'public' + _inheritrights:true body, no display_order in create body per its own doc comment lines 58-60), :345-415 (reorderSections — GET existing display_order value id -> ONE atomic overwrite POST 1-based renumber per #264 pattern), :465-488 (deleteSection — two parallel emptiness-count GETs before DELETE entity/{id}), :623-659 (renameSection — same GET-then-atomic-POST-overwrite idiom). Host pages: repertoire CRUD is wired into src/routes/+page.svelte (createRepertoireItem call at line 1616, deleteRepertoireItem at 1680/1804) rendered via src/lib/components/agenda/RepertoireElement.svelte; section CRUD is wired into src/routes/roster/+page.svelte.
findings.implication: For #256's link entity (collective-scoped, wants manual arrangement per the issue's own sketch: 'display_order for manual arrangement'), sectionActions.ts's create+reorder+delete triad (atomic-overwrite renumber pattern) is the nearer structural fit than repertoire_item's simpler no-reorder CRUD; repertoire_item is the nearer fit only for 'no manual ordering needed' scope.

findings.claim: Admin-only edit-gating uses two distinct idioms depending on surface: rights-derived `manageRights === 'editor'` (repertoire/programme) vs. `$adminStore`-derived owner/editor tier checks (sections/roster).
findings.evidence: src/lib/components/agenda/RepertoireElement.svelte:250-256 derives `canManageRepertoire`/`canManageProgramme` from `(seasonRights ?? manageRights) === 'editor'`, gating template blocks at lines 541, 574, 680. src/routes/roster/+page.svelte:28,66,74 imports `adminStore`/`resolveOwnerTier` and derives `const admin = $derived($adminStore)`; section create/reorder/delete controls key off `_owner`/`_editor` tiers read via that store (comments at lines 87-89, 942-970, 3868-3871, 4293-4301). Both ultimately trace to the same underlying Entu rights props (`_owner`/`_editor`) via `manageRightsFrom`/`resolveManageRights` (repertoireActions.ts:291-335), just surfaced through a season/event-scoped derived value on one page vs. a store-level derived value on the other.
findings.implication: A future links surface must pick which idiom its host page already uses (per-entity manageRightsFrom if hosted alongside repertoire/agenda, or adminStore-style tier if hosted alongside roster/admin) rather than inventing a third pattern.

findings.claim: i18n key naming is NOT one uniform convention — it is domain-prefixed (`repertoire_*`) on the agenda-hosted surface and route+entity-prefixed (`roster_section_*`) on the roster-hosted surface.
findings.evidence: `grep -o '"repertoire_[a-z_]*"' messages/en.json` yields flat `repertoire_add_work_button`, `repertoire_move_up`, `repertoire_manage_error`, etc. (domain word only, no route prefix — repertoire spans multiple routes/components). `grep -o '"roster_[a-z_]*section[a-z_]*"' messages/en.json` yields `roster_section_create_failed`, `roster_section_reorder_failed`, `roster_section_remove_confirm`, `roster_new_section`, etc. (route prefix `roster_` + entity noun `section_` + action).
findings.implication: A links surface's key prefix should mirror whichever page hosts it (e.g. `admin_link_*` or `collective_link_*` if admin-hosted, `links_*` if it gets its own route) rather than assuming either existing convention applies uniformly — this is a placement decision the args should make explicit, not inherit implicitly.

findings.claim: Nothing for #256's link/lingikogu feature exists in the app yet: no route, no data-helper module, no i18n keys, no nav entry.
findings.evidence: `find src -iname "*link*"` and `grep -rn "'link'|link_collection|lingikogu" -ri src messages` (excluding node_modules) surfaced only the pre-existing, unrelated OAuth account-linking flow (`intent: 'link'` in src/lib/auth/state.ts:18, src/routes/auth/[provider]/build-oauth-init-url.ts, src/routes/auth/callback/run-callback-exchange.ts:54, src/routes/profile/+page.svelte:664) plus the CSS/typography token literal `'link'` in src/typography-scale.spec.ts:45 — none are the link-collection entity from issue #256. src/lib/nav/entries.ts:29-72 (NAV_ENTRIES) is a fixed 6-item array (agenda/roster/profile/library/admin/collectives) with no links row and no gating slot reserved for one.
findings.implication: The eventual UI-slice implementer must scaffold everything from scratch — data helper (lib/links/linksData.ts + linksActions.ts, by analogy), a host page or NAV_ENTRIES addition, and a fresh i18n prefix — and must NOT assume any existing route/helper/key stub is waiting to be filled in. Issue #256 itself is still gated on a PO governance ruling (app-extension vs. canonical v4E type) per its own body, so this app-side scan is prep-only, not a green light to start the UI slice.
